## Summary

I hardened the zip extraction logic in `python/ray/_private/runtime_env/packaging.py` against path traversal and absolute-path attacks.

**New helpers** (module-level, before `remove_dir_from_filepaths`):
- `_is_absolute_path(path)` — detects both Unix-style (`/foo`) and Windows-style (`C:/foo`, `C:\foo`, `\foo`) absolute paths regardless of host OS, so a malicious archive crafted on one platform is caught on another.
- `_resolved_path_within_dir(path, directory)` — containment check using `os.path.realpath` (via the module-level `import os`, so tests can patch `packaging_module.os.path.realpath`).

**`unzip_package`** — replaced the fragile `os.path.commonpath` check with:
- Per-entry skip when `_is_absolute_path(member)` or the entry's realpath escapes `target_dir`. Crucially, the write path (`member_path`) is still built from the original `target_dir`, never from the realpath-resolved directory.
- The top-level-directory stripping only runs when the detected top-level dir is a safe, contained subdirectory that was actually extracted — so when *every* entry is unsafe (nothing extracted), no move happens and no external files are touched.

**`remove_dir_from_filepaths`** — now raises `ValueError` up front when `rdir` is `""`, `"."`, `".."`, or any absolute path (Unix or Windows), guarding its internal `shutil.move` from operating outside `base_dir`.

**Verification:**
- Custom sanity tests: mixed safe/unsafe entries (safe extracted, all traversal/absolute variants skipped and no external files created), all-unsafe + `remove_top_level_directory=True` (nothing extracted, no crash, externals untouched), `ValueError` guards, `realpath` patched via module `os` (files still land at original path), and normal top-level removal — all pass.
- Existing suite: 16 relevant tests (`Unzip`, `RemoveDir`, `TopLevel`, `traversal`) all pass.

I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
